prompt: What happens to the planner a few seconds after the person switches to another app?
hint: It is not a computer's window.

choices.text: It keeps running at a lower priority
choices.why: That is a computer's behaviour; iOS suspends it.

choices.text: It is suspended, in memory, using no processor
choices.why: Right, and it may be removed from memory when room is needed.

choices.text: It is closed and loses everything not on the server
choices.why: It is suspended first; and the device's file keeps what was saved.

choices.text: It refreshes its data every fifteen minutes
choices.why: Only if the system grants a refresh task, when it chooses.

prompt: According to Apple's documentation, up to how many seconds of runtime does an app refresh task get?
hint: The same number appears for a background push.

prompt: The planner sets `earliestBeginDate` to six in the morning. What does that promise?
hint: Read the documentation's sentence about it.

choices.text: That the refresh runs at six, give or take a minute
choices.why: The system does not guarantee launching at that date.

choices.text: That it runs at six if the phone is charging
choices.why: Charging is a processing task's condition, and it promises nothing either.

choices.text: Only that it will not begin before six
choices.why: Right: the system chooses when, and it may be many hours later.

choices.text: That the app will be woken at six to show a notification
choices.why: A refresh shows nothing; notifications are lesson 17.

prompt: Match each need to what to ask the system for.

pairs.left: Refresh the plan now and then
Clean a database overnight on the charger
A large download that should finish while suspended
An export the person starts and watches, on iOS 26

prompt: `BGTaskScheduler.shared.submit(request)` throws `notPermitted`. What are the two causes Apple's documentation gives?
hint: Two lists in the app's configuration.

choices.text: The device is in Low Power Mode, or the app is in the foreground
choices.why: Neither is what `notPermitted` means.

choices.text: A background mode or an identifier missing from its lists
choices.why: Right: both are in the app's declaration.

choices.text: Too many requests, or an `earliestBeginDate` in the past
choices.why: Too many requests is a different error.

choices.text: The person has not granted permission in Settings
choices.why: Refresh tasks ask the person nothing.

prompt: Why does the planner's refresh handler call `scheduleRefresh` before it returns?
hint: How many times does one request run?

choices.text: To extend the current task's 30 seconds
choices.why: Nothing extends the current task.

choices.text: Because the system refuses to run a handler that schedules nothing
choices.why: No such rule; the cost is quieter.

choices.text: A refresh request runs once
choices.why: Right: without it, the app refreshes in the background exactly once.

choices.text: To cancel the request the app made when it launched
choices.why: A new request with the same identifier replaces the old; it is not a cancellation.

prompt: What happens, according to Apple's documentation, when the `backgroundTask` closure has not returned by the time the task runs out?
hint: It is something Swift code can notice.

choices.text: The system cancels the task
choices.why: Right: ordinary Swift cancellation, which section 07 practises.

choices.text: The system waits for it and then shortens the next refresh
choices.why: It does not wait.

choices.text: The app is shown a dialog asking whether to keep running
choices.why: Nobody is asked; the person is not even looking.

choices.text: The work is moved to a processing task overnight
choices.why: Nothing is moved; it is cancelled.

prompt: Which request property asks the system to wait for a charger?

choices.text: `earliestBeginDate`
choices.why: That is a time, not power.

choices.text: `requiresExternalPower`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `requiresNetworkConnectivity`
choices.why: That is the network.

choices.text: `isDiscretionary`
choices.why: That belongs to a background URL session's configuration.

prompt: Why does the planner, as written, have little use for a processing task?

choices.text: Processing tasks are refused to apps under 50 MB
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: Its store is one small file with nothing to compact or rebuild
choices.why: Right: asking for time it does not need costs battery for nothing.

choices.text: It already does all its work in `BGContinuedProcessingTask`
choices.why: It targets iOS 17, where that task does not exist.

choices.text: Processing tasks cannot reach the network
choices.why: They can, with `requiresNetworkConnectivity`.

prompt: What does Apple's documentation require of a `BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest` at submission?

choices.text: That the device is charging
choices.why: That is a processing request's option.

choices.text: That it is submitted from the background at night
choices.why: The opposite: from the foreground.

choices.text: That it comes from the foreground, as a result of something the person did
choices.why: Right, such as tapping a button.

choices.text: That the app has no other task pending
choices.why: Not a stated requirement.

prompt: Why does a background `URLSession` use a delegate instead of the `async` methods from lesson 12?
hint: Where is the app while the transfer finishes?

choices.text: Because `async` methods are slower for large files
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: It finishes after the app has left memory
choices.why: Right: an `await` needs the app alive; the system calls the delegate after relaunching it.

choices.text: Because delegates are required on Linux
choices.why: Background sessions are not on Linux at all.

choices.text: To let the person cancel from a notification
choices.why: Nothing in a background session does that.

prompt: Which part of the planner would justify a background session?

choices.text: Sending each session added offline
choices.why: A few dozen bytes; ordinary requests in a refresh fit.

choices.text: Refreshing the list of courses each morning
choices.why: Small JSON; an app refresh task fits.

choices.text: Downloading a year of study as a file
choices.why: Right: a large transfer the person need not wait for.

choices.text: Showing a course cover
choices.why: A cover is wanted on screen now, not later.

prompt: With three sessions waiting at 22:30, when does the planner's rule ask for the next refresh?
hint: The person's work is not on the server.

choices.text: At six the next morning
choices.why: That is the rule with nothing waiting.
Right: fifteen minutes later.

choices.text: Immediately, at 22:30
choices.why: The rule asks for fifteen minutes later, and the system may wait longer.

choices.text: At midnight, when the day changes
choices.why: Nothing in the rule mentions midnight.

prompt: Lisbon, 22:30 on 24 October 2026, nothing waiting: how many minutes until the next refresh, as `background` printed?
hint: The clocks go back that night.

prompt: Why does `nextRefresh` use `calendar.nextDate(after:matching:)` instead of adding the hours until six to the current time?

choices.text: Adding seconds to a `Date` is not allowed in Swift
choices.why: It is; the pending rule adds 900 seconds.

choices.text: To make the result independent of the time zone
choices.why: The opposite: it uses the calendar's time zone deliberately.

choices.text: It knows the night the clocks change; a sum would give five o'clock
choices.why: Right: that night is an hour longer, and the calendar counted it.

choices.text: Because six o'clock is not a whole number of hours away
choices.why: Half hours are easy to add; the clock change is the problem.

prompt: Why does `syncUntilCancelled` save after every session instead of once at the end?

choices.text: Because `FileStore` can only hold one session per write
choices.why: It writes the whole snapshot each time.

choices.text: So a task cut off midway keeps what it already sent
choices.why: Right: otherwise those sessions would stay pending and be sent again.

choices.text: To make the server log each one separately
choices.why: The server logs each post anyway.

choices.text: Because saving is what triggers the next post
choices.why: The loop triggers the next post.

prompt: Each `background run 1.0` sent how many sessions before it was cancelled?
In the first run, `b3`'s post was cut off by the cancellation. What happened to `b3`?

choices.text: It was dropped, like a refused session
choices.why: Only a 4xx drops a session; cancellation keeps it.

choices.text: It was marked as sent, since its post had started
choices.why: Only a success moves it across.

choices.text: It stayed pending and went first in the next run
choices.why: Right: the second run sent `b3` and `b4`.

choices.text: It was sent twice, once in each run
choices.why: The server logged six posts for six sessions.

prompt: To run code the moment cancellation arrives, Apple's documentation suggests wrapping the work in `with___CancellationHandler`.
Where do Apple's `_simulateLaunchForTaskWithIdentifier` and `_simulateExpirationForTaskWithIdentifier` commands work?

choices.text: On a device, typed at the debugger's prompt
choices.why: Right: only on devices, per the guide.

choices.text: In the simulator, from a menu
choices.why: The guide says they work only on devices.

choices.text: In the app's code, behind `#if DEBUG`
choices.why: Referencing them in submitted code is cause for rejection; they are typed, not written.

choices.text: On Linux, with `swift test`
choices.why: They are calls into Apple's scheduler.

prompt: How does `aCancelledSyncSendsNothingAndKeepsEverything` make the cancellation certain rather than a matter of timing?

choices.text: It sleeps for one second before cancelling
choices.why: A sleep would be timing, the thing it avoids.

choices.text: It uses `SlowSource` with a longer delay
choices.why: The test uses `FakeSource`, with no delay.

choices.text: `withUnsafeCurrentTask` cancels the running task before the sync starts
choices.why: Right: the sync sees a cancelled task on its first check.

choices.text: It switches `FakeSource` offline
choices.why: That would test offline, not cancellation.

choices.text: Three one-second runs of `syncUntilCancelled`
choices.why: Yes: section 07.

choices.text: The `_simulateExpiration…` debugger command
choices.why: No: devices only, not run.
